answer: A new key becomes voting-eligible only after it plants a locked bond on a public knoll and holds it unmoved until the next epoch horizon. An established key may sponsor at most one newcomer per epoch, and only if its own bond stays visible across that horizon. The sponsorship graph is stained violet when two newcomers share timing, transit, or derivation patterns; every sponsor and newcomer in that component is slashed. Standing up k sockpuppets therefore costs k locked bonds plus k unique unstained sponsors, so capital and social cost grow linearly and one shared fingerprint burns the clique.
